nodes.label: Overhead Broiler House CCTV Frame 05701
nodes.description: Raw, unannotated top-down surveillance still extracted from commercial broiler-house video. Shows several hundred white broiler chickens densely packed on a litter/dirt floor, a horizontal suspended feed pipe carrying five red-and-white circular pan feeders across the middle of the frame, and a dark drinker/nipple line curving across the lower third. Burnt-in overlays: '1080P-IPC-Siren' (camera/stream identity, top-left) and '2022-03-01 23:05:03' (top-right). This is pipeline input data, not model output — the img_test directory supplies real deployment frames for chicken detection and behavior analysis.
nodes.rationale: A fixed ceiling-mounted camera was chosen over ground-level cameras because it yields near-constant scale and unobstructed coverage of the whole pen, which is what makes per-bird counting and spatial (feeder-proximity) behavior scoring tractable.

nodes.label: Dense Flock Occlusion and Small-Object Regime
nodes.description: The visual regime the detector must survive: hundreds of near-identical white birds at low pixel-area each, heavily overlapping and touching, against a low-contrast grey litter background, with birds partially hidden under feeder pans and behind the feed pipe. Individuals are separable mainly by body-axis orientation and shadow gaps rather than by colour or texture.
nodes.rationale: This is the hardest case for both the detector (small, low-contrast, class-uniform objects) and the tracker (identity switches when boxes overlap), and it explains why a dedicated fine-tuned model is needed rather than off-the-shelf COCO weights.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder and Drinker Line as Spatial Landmarks
nodes.description: Fixed house infrastructure visible in every frame: five circular pan feeders on a rigid horizontal pipe, plus a drinker line lower in the frame. Birds visibly cluster in rosettes around each pan. Because the camera is static, these structures occupy constant image coordinates and can serve as reference regions.
nodes.rationale: Feeder and drinker positions are stable across the whole recording, so feeding/drinking behavior can be scored geometrically (bird centroid inside or near a feeder region) instead of requiring a separate learned behavior classifier.

nodes.label: Burnt-in Camera ID and Timestamp Overlay
nodes.description: Non-removable pixel overlay rendered by the IP camera itself: stream label '1080P-IPC-Siren' and wall-clock timestamp '2022-03-01 23:05:03'. It anchors each extracted frame to absolute time (here a night-time recording under artificial light), enabling diurnal behavior analysis, but it also injects high-contrast text into the image that a detector may hallucinate on.
nodes.rationale: Keeping the burnt-in timestamp trades a small risk of spurious detections in the overlay corners for the ability to align frame indices with real clock time without a separate metadata sidecar.

nodes.label: Fixed Top-Down Viewpoint
nodes.description: The nadir/near-nadir camera geometry of the target domain: no perspective foreshortening between foreground and background, negligible scale variation across the frame, no horizon, and object appearance dominated by rotation in the image plane. Contrasts sharply with the ground-level, strong-perspective viewpoint of the bundled tracker and detector demo assets.
nodes.rationale: Constant object scale removes the need for heavy multi-scale reasoning but makes rotation invariance the dominant requirement, so demo assets shot from ground level are a poor proxy for expected accuracy on this domain.
